title: tool-execution-coordinator: deterministic ordering, optimistic result-injection, and per-tool retry policies
author: Priya Kapoor
release_notes: Adds a ToolExecutionCoordinator to coordinate multi-tool invocations with deterministic ordering and per-tool retry/backoff policies; introduces optimistic result injection to improve latency for common fast-path tools; SDK compatibility bumps and docs for new orchestration flags.
description:
Context and motivation: Multi-tool workloads revealed two classes of flakiness in production: (1) nondeterministic ordering when the model invoked multiple tools in a single plan, which made downstream structured-output validation brittle, and (2) transient tool failures that either caused the whole plan to abort or resulted in inconsistent partial outputs. This PR implements a runtime-level Coordinator to make multi-tool execution deterministic and resilient.

Design summary: The ToolExecutionCoordinator is an orchestrator sitting between the API surface and individual tool runners. Key behaviors: deterministic ordering (tools are executed according to the model-declared plan unless an explicit parallel hint is present), optimistic result-injection (race-safe fast-path where quick-success tools can inject results back into the generation stream before full plumbing completes), and per-tool retry policies with jittered exponential backoff and idempotency guards. The coordinator exposes a small set of controls into the public API: orchestration_mode (deterministic|parallel|optimistic), tool_retry_policy (none|default|aggressive), and injection_ttl_ms (how long optimistic injected results remain valid).

Compatibility: This is an API-surface change but backwards-compatible by default: the default mode remains deterministic with conservative retry semantics to match existing behavior. The SDKs are bumped to accept the new orchestration flags; the OpenAI-compat layer maps function-calling hints to orchestration_mode when present (e.g., "x-openai-parallel": true -> orchestration_mode=parallel). Streaming and structured output: optimistic injection is designed to work with streaming responses — injected results are emitted as structured tokens (function_call events) so client streaming handlers can validate partial outputs. Structured output schemas are validated against the existing schema validators after ordering reconciliation.

Commits (summary): add coordinator core and tests; implement optimistic injection plumbing; add per-tool retry policy and config; SDK: expose orchestration flags (js + py); docs: orchestration guide and examples; fix: race condition in KV cache invalidation when optimistic injection occurs.

Changed files (high level): redwood/runtime/coordinator/ToolExecutionCoordinator.rs; redwood/runtime/coordinator/README.md; redwood/api/handler/tool_orchestration.go; redwood/sdk-typescript/src/orchestration.ts; redwood/sdk-python/redwood/orchestration.py; redwood/docs/orchestration.md; redwood/tests/integration/test_tool_coordinator.py; redwood/runtime/tests/test_injection_race.rs; redwood/benchmarks/tool-orchestration-latency.yaml.

Notable implementation details: - Coordinator uses a lightweight vector clock per-plan to deterministically order tool completions when model plan indicates strict ordering. - Optimistic injection path uses a short-lived KV lease to ensure injected tokens are not double-applied; the lease is revoked if the authoritative tool result later disagrees and reconciliation uses a patch event. - Retries are applied only to idempotent tools by default; non-idempotent tools must opt in via tool metadata or the orchestration_mode. - Added metrics: coordinator.plan_latency_ms, coordinator.retry_count, coordinator.injection_conflicts. These are surfaced to Console and included in per-route breakdowns.

Review conversation (high level):
- Ethan Liu: "Nice separation of concerns. A couple of questions: how do we guarantee we won't break streaming parsers that assume monotonic token order? Can optimistic injection interleave with partial text tokens?"
- Priya (author): "We only inject structured function_call events, never mid-token text. The coordinator produces explicit 'injection' event types that SDK streaming handlers map to the existing function_call stream event; we'll add a compatibility layer in the JS SDK to translate older handlers."
- María González: "Can we avoid default retries for popular non-idempotent payment lookup tools?"
- Priya: "Yes — non-idempotent tools are excluded by default; we added a tool metadata flag 'allow_retries'. We also documented how to mark a tool safe for retries."
- Samir Patel (request changes): "The initial KV lease approach looked racy when coordinator restarts happen mid-plan. Please add a test simulating restart and ensure lease recovery works."
- Priya: "Added test_injection_recovery and improved lease recovery logic; included a migration note for existing deployments to enable coordinator state checkpoints."
- Samir: "LGTM after the additional test was added and the documentation was clarified."

CI summary: All CI jobs passed once the integration tests were stabilized. One flaky test (test_tool_coordinator_timeout) failed on first run and was retried; subsequent runs passed. Benchmarks: microbenchmark shows median tool-latency improvement of ~18% for common fast-path tools when optimistic injection is enabled.

Rollout and deployment notes: Coordinator is behind a runtime feature flag (runtime.orchestration_v2) and defaults to off for Private installers older than 2025-07-01. SRE playbook updated with a rollback step to disable optimistic injection if we observe injection_conflicts > 0.1% for a route.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged to main on 2025-08-02 after approvals from reviewers and green CI.

Follow-ups and open items: - Backfill additional end-to-end tests for OpenAI compatibility layer when clients stream function_call events concurrently with tool results (ENG-8420). - Add a small sample in quickstarts showing mixing blocking and parallel tools with orchestration_mode=optimistic. - Investigate coordinator-level request-level throttling to reduce retries under heavy contention.
